newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Body of Busang geologist to undergo autopsy.
newsitem.headline: Body of Busang geologist to undergo autopsy.

text.p: Indonesian doctors were due to perform an autopsy on Tuesday on the body of geologist Michael de Guzman, who fell from a helicopter while flying to the Busang gold property he helped discover in East Kalimantan province.
Sugianto, chief of the airport in the East Kalimantan capital of Samarinda, said de Guzman's body was at a public hospital in the provincial capital.

"Doctors will do an autopsy on the body today," he told Reuters by telephone. Sugianto was involved in the search and rescue operations launched after de Guzman fell from the Alouette 3 helicopter last week.
"The body seems to be fairly intact," he added.

Sugianto said last Friday that de Guzman may have committed suicide as one of several letters found in a bag he had left behind in the helicopter was addressed to his wife saying that he was suffering from acute hepatitis B.

De Guzman, a Philippines national, was on his way to the Busang property last Wednesday when the back door of the helicopter burst open 17 minutes after leaving Samarinda airport, search and rescue officials said.

The Busang motherlode, estimated by Canadian exploration company Bre-X Minerals Ltd to contain at least 71 million ounces of gold currently worth around $25 billion, is the biggest gold find this century.
The helicopter had been hired by Bre-X, where de Guzman was chief geologist, and was said to be in good condition.
Frank Cimafranca, third secretary and consul at the Philippine embassy in Jakarta, confirmed the autopsy would take place on Tuesday.
He said de Guzman's body was likely to be shipped back to the Philippines over the next few days unless police wanted to conduct further investigations.
Embassy sources said de Guzman's wife and two daughters were expected to arrive in Jakarta on Thursday from the Philippines. The sources did not rule out a further autopsy.
Bre-X has entered into an an agreement with Indonesian partners and the U.S. mining giant Freeport McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc to develop Busang.

The death of de Guzman coupled with an Indonesian newspaper report last Friday that Busang contained less than the estimated gold reserves hit Bre-X share prices on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday, analysts said.
The shares rebounded partly on Monday after the company issued a statement defending the accuracy of the assay results and calculations on the amount of gold contained in Busang.
